=You are the art director who writes cover-image prompts for technical articles (the prompt goes to an AI image model). Write one specific, editorial cover-image prompt that is directly tied to the title below.

ARTICLE TITLE: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.title }}
CATEGORY: {{ $('Category + Format Rotation').first().json.category_name }}
FORMAT: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.format_name }}

ANALYZE INTERNALLY FIRST
- Pick the main technical object/actor in the title.
- Pick the action and relationship in the title: flow, splitting, compression, monitoring, comparison, latency, scaling, debugging, etc.
- Build one single visual metaphor; do not turn unrelated technology icons into a collage.
- Objects and scene must be specific enough that someone who read the title would recognize the topic.

CATEGORY-SPECIFIC GUIDANCE
- AI/ML/computer vision: camera sensor, abstract image layers, bounding-box-like geometric frames, inference pipeline, model layers; no random robots or brains.
- Backend/API/streaming: request flow, queues, router nodes, abstract data paths without dashboards; no server racks or hackers.
- Database/query: data tables, index tree, query paths and a visual metaphor of selected records; no generic database server.
- Frontend/mobile: component layers, responsive surfaces, device frames and render flow; no random code screens.
- Hardware/deployment: edge device, model flow on a chip, energy/heat or quantization layers; no generic GPU photo.

VISUAL LANGUAGE
- Premium technical magazine cover, 16:9 landscape, one main focal point, strong negative space.
- Pick 2-3 colors that suit the topic; do not repeat the same blue neon network aesthetic in every post.
- Photorealistic editorial still life or a controlled 3D conceptual scene; choose based on the topic.
- No text, letters, numbers, logos, brands, watermarks, readable UI, real code, human faces or cliché hacker scenes.
- No overly abstract, generic or unrelated technology imagery.
- Do not add products/brands/technologies that are not in the title.

OUTPUT: only the image prompt, in English. 2 sentences, 55-90 words. Specify composition, main object, action/metaphor, material, lighting, color, camera and the 16:9 aspect ratio. No explanation or quotation marks.

=You are an experienced engineer and technical writer writing for {{ $('Config').first().json.audience }}. Based on the research brief below, write a blog post that ranks well in search and is genuinely useful to the reader. Write the article in {{ $('Config').first().json.language }}. Your output is pure JSON. TODAY: {{ $now.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd') }} DRAFT TITLE: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.title }} FOCUS KEYWORD: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.focus_keyword }} SECONDARY KEYWORDS: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.secondary_keywords.join(', ') }} TARGET READER: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.target_reader }} WHY NOW: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.why_now }} FORMAT: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.format_name }} FORMAT GUIDE: {{ $('Pick Topic').first().json.format_guide }} RESEARCH BRIEF (your source of current, verified information) {{ $('Extract Brief').first().json.brief }} INTERNAL LINK CANDIDATES (existing posts on the blog) {{ $('Category + Format Rotation').first().json.internal_links }} CONTENT RULES 1. Search intent: the first 2-3 sentences of the introduction answer the reader's question DIRECTLY (clear enough to be quoted in featured snippets and AI Overviews). The focus keyword appears naturally within the first 100 words; secondary keywords are spread naturally across h2/h3 headings and the text. No keyword stuffing. 2. Freshness and accuracy: write versions, dates, statistics and API names ONLY based on the brief. Do NOT invent numbers, benchmarks or "company X experienced this" stories that are not in the brief. Do not present old models, versions or product names as current. 3. Depth: {{ $('Config').first().json.target_words_min }}-{{ $('Config').first().json.target_words_max }} words. No padding; every section teaches the reader something new. Always cover the angles that the "competitor analysis" in the brief says are missing. 4. Practicality: {{ $('Config').first().json.require_code_example === false ? 'at least 2 concrete, realistic, practical examples' : 'at least 2 working, realistic code or configuration examples (with short explanations)' }}. A comparison or decision table where it fits, and always an implementation checklist. 5. Trade-offs: include a "When not to use it / what are the alternatives" section. 6. Internal links: link to 2-3 posts from the list above that are GENUINELY related, with natural anchor text inside a sentence: .... If no post is related, do not force it. 7. External links: link to 1-3 of the official documentation URLs from the brief. Never invent URLs that are not in the brief. 8. FAQ: write 4-6 of the reader questions from the brief as h3 question + p answer; each answer 40-70 words, its first sentence answers directly. 9. Tone: like an experienced engineer explaining something to a colleague; clear, concrete, plain {{ $('Config').first().json.language }}. Invented personal experience ("we ran into this in our project", "in my 15 years of experience") is FORBIDDEN. 10. FORBIDDEN PHRASES (and their equivalents in {{ $('Config').first().json.language }}): {{ ($('Config').first().json.banned_phrases || []).map(p => '"' + p + '"').join(', ') }}. 11. Paragraphs have at most 4 sentences. Break long blocks of text into lists, tables or subheadings. STRUCTURE (adapt to the format)

Introduction: 2-3 short paragraphs, direct answer + why it matters.

"Table of contents", written in {{ $('Config').first().json.language }}

— a
    with anchor links to the h2 sections (give every h2 a short ASCII id:

    ). 4-6 main h2 sections (headings match search intent and contain a question or the keyword where possible), h3 where needed.

    "Frequently asked questions", written in {{ $('Config').first().json.language }}

    "Conclusion", written in {{ $('Config').first().json.language }}

    — 1-2 paragraph summary and a clear next step. HTML RULES - NO Markdown, HTML only. Do not use h1. - Code: 
    ...
    ; escape <, >, & inside code as < > &. - Lists
      /
        , emphasis /, tables ......
        , important warnings
        . OUTPUT FORMAT — only valid JSON (NO code fence, NO explanation): { "title": "45-70 characters; focus keyword in the first half of the title; clear benefit; no invented numbers", "excerpt": "140-160 character meta description; contains the focus keyword and invites the click", "slug": "3-6 words, lowercase, ASCII, hyphen-separated (e.g. docker-compose-tutorial)", "tags": ["3-5 readable tags in their natural spelling (e.g. \"Claude Code\", \"Docker\", \"PostgreSQL\") — not slug format"], "content": "the full HTML content" } - Your reply starts with { and ends with }. Escape double quotes inside content as \" and line breaks as \n.

## Grounded Blog Writer — setup
**1. Credentials** (open each node with a warning):
- **Google Gemini(PaLM) API** → 3 Gemini model nodes + 3 Gemini HTTP nodes
- **Basic Auth** = WordPress username + *Application Password* → Fetch Last 50 Posts, Upload Featured Image, Get or Create Tag, Create Post
- **SMTP** → both mail nodes
- *optional* **Google Service Account API** with "Set up for use in HTTP Request node" ON and scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/indexing` → Google Indexing API

**2. Edit `Config`**: site URL, language, audience, categories, formats, models, mail.

**3. Test**: set `post_status` to `draft`, run once, read the mail + the draft. Then switch to `publish` and activate.

Runs **Tuesday 06:00** in the workflow timezone (Settings → Timezone or `GENERIC_TIMEZONE`).

### 1 · Research
Last 50 posts → category/format rotation + overused-tech blacklist → trend signals (HN, dev.to, GitHub, Reddit) → 6 **Google-grounded** topic candidates → **Google Autocomplete demand score** + overlap check → grounded **research brief**

### 2 · Write
Cover image prompt + image → draft → **Number Check** (numbers that are not in the brief) → editor pass → **Quality Gate** (editor version, else draft, else stop — nothing is published)

### 3 · Publish & index
Upload cover (alt text) → get/create tags → create post (slug, tags, featured image) → optional deploy hook → Google Indexing API (optional) → IndexNow (optional) → report mail. Tag/image failures only produce warnings; a failed post creation sends the fail mail.
